recipe: Type your ref by passing a three.js class through useRef's generics, and append a non-null assertion (null!) to tell TypeScript that ref.current is defined when accessed in effects or useFrame.
trigger_condition: You are using useRef to reference a three.js element (e.g., Mesh) in a React Three Fiber component.
evidence: You can type the ref yourself by passing a type through `useRef`'s generics

recipe: Use the ThreeElements interface to extract the type of a specific three.js element and intersect it with your own props to type a component that spreads three.js props.
trigger_condition: You want to spread props or type a component that relies on three.js elements.
evidence: Whenever you want to spread props or type components that rely on three elements, you can use the `ThreeElements` interface to extract the mesh, group, or any other three element, including custom elements.

recipe: Call extend() from @react-three/fiber with your custom three.js class to register it in the reconciler's catalogue so it can be used as a JSX element.
trigger_condition: You need to use a third-party or custom three.js element within a React Three Fiber scene.
evidence: react-three-fiber can also accept third-party elements and extend them into its internal catalogue.

recipe: Declare a module augmentation for @react-three/fiber's ThreeElements interface, mapping your custom element name to ThreeElement<typeof YourClass>, so TypeScript recognizes the element in JSX.
trigger_condition: TypeScript does not recognize a custom extended element in JSX after calling extend().
evidence: To define our element in JSX, we'll use the `ThreeElement` interface to extend `ThreeElements`.

recipe: Use the extend factory signature (const Element = extend(CustomElement)) instead of the object form, which automatically infers types locally and prevents namespace bleeding.
trigger_condition: You are creating a custom three.js element and want TypeScript to infer its types without manual module augmentation.
evidence: You can shorten element definition by using the `extend` factory signature, which will automatically extend the element locally.
source_name: React Three Fiber v10 docs: TypeScript

recipe: Call extend(THREE) with the entire three.js namespace when opening your own root via createRoot, since extend accepts it as-is and registers only constructors without needing a cast.
trigger_condition: You are opening your own root instead of using the Canvas component and want all three.js elements available as JSX.
evidence: If you open your own root instead of using `<Canvas>`, you can extend the default elements with `extend`.
